confirmed.title: Opening a video by single-page navigation shows a generic view titled 'YouTube' above the player for 2-8 s, then jumps to the real layout
confirmed.where: YouTube: clicking a video or Mix in Sift on search results or home (single-page navigation to /watch)
confirmed.evidence: Polled every 100 ms after the click (t1r6/spapoll.ts), 3 of 3 navigations. Search -> Mix: 'h1=YouTube@96 portal=144 seek=false first=h1.,figure.portal-wrap' from 3.9 s to 12.1 s. Search -> video (pp= link): from 1.9 s to 4.2 s. Home -> Mix: from 1.7 s to 6.3 s. Then the layout switches to the player at 95 with the real H1 below it at 633 (a jump of about 540 px for the title). In this interim view the seek slider and the metadata are missing. The adapter view lands exactly when the original's #title h1 fills, so only the interim view is wrong. The original shows an empty title area in that window, not 'YouTube'. On fresh loads this no longer happens (F309). Shots: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-1/research/shots/R6T1-spa-youtube-h1-1.png, R6T1-spa-youtube-h1-0.png, contact sheet R6T1-spa-contact.png.
confirmed.repro: cd /home/nico/projects/sift-test-1; SIFT_PORT=9461 SIFT_PORT=9461 SIFT_TAB=T1-youtube bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/t1r6/spapoll.ts 'https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=rick+astley' 'main li a.title[href*="dQw4w9WgXcQ"]' 14000. It prints 'h1=YouTube@96 portal=144 ... first=h1.,figure.portal-wrap' for several seconds before 'h1=Rick Astley - ...@633 portal=95'. Also try 'https://www.youtube.com/' with the same selector.
confirmed.suspectedCause: After a single-page navigation, watch() in src/content/adapters/youtube.ts returns null while the watch metadata is not ready, and the generic extractor renders document.title ('YouTube' during YouTube's navigation) as the H1. watchSettling() and the early-title path appear to cover only the first load.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced in 3 of 3 single-page navigations with T1's spapoll.ts. Search to Mix: h1=YouTube@96 from 155 ms to 3081 ms, with the portal at 144 once it appears. Search to the second video: the same from 240 ms to 3564 ms. Home to Mix: the same from 148 ms to 2856 ms. Each time the view then switched to the player at 95 and the real H1 at 633. During that window the original's ytd-watch-metadata #title h1 was empty. In one run document.title already named the video at 1389 ms, but the H1 still said 'YouTube'. The suspected cause is wrong. The generic extractor is not involved. The YouTube adapter makes this view itself. With no title yet, watch() in src/content/adapters/youtube.ts returns a partial page: in the !flexy branch it is base([loading], 'YouTube'), and in the flexy branch it is base([player], ... || 'YouTube'), with no title block in either. App() in src/content/ui/app.tsx then draws page.title as a separate h1 (showTitle) above the blocks. When the title arrives, the H1 moves below the player. This is a real layout jump of about 540 px on every video opened in place, plus a wrong heading.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/adapters/youtube.ts watch(), for the partial page with no title (the !flexy branch when not on first load, and the !fresh branch), do not fall back to 'YouTube' as page.title. Pass an empty title, so App() draws no stand-alone h1, or put the title-keyed h block after the player (use docTitle once it no longer reads 'YouTube' or the previous page's title). Then the H1 stays below the player and does not jump.

Home -> Mix: 'YouTube' at 973 ms, and the region still said 'YouTube' about 20 s later. Home -> another video: 'YouTube' at 412 ms. By contrast, a search announces 'Search: rick astley' and Back announces 'Home' correctly (t1r6/announce3.ts). A screen-reader user who opens a video never hears which video opened.
confirmed.repro: cd /home/nico/projects/sift-test-1; SIFT_PORT=9461 SIFT_TAB=T1-youtube bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/t1r6/announce2.ts 'https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=rick+astley' 'main li a.title[href*="dQw4w9WgXcQ"][href*="pp="]' 14000. It prints the status text changes ('YouTube' only) and the final document.title (the video's title).
confirmed.suspectedCause: src/content/index.ts around lines 1638-1652. On navigation, page.title is YouTube's placeholder 'YouTube'. From search it differs from prevTitle, so 'YouTube' is said at once and titleWait is false. From home, prevTitle is also 'YouTube', so the 2.5 s timer fires while the title is still the placeholder. The real title, which arrives 4-12 s later, is never said.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced twice with T1's announce2.ts. Home to Mix: the polite region said only 'YouTube' at 520 ms. Search to the 'Never Gonna Give You Up' video: only 'YouTube' at 630 ms. After 12-14 s, document.title was the full video title, and Sift's H1 had shown it since about 3 s, but nothing more was announced. The code matches. In src/content/index.ts (navigation branch around lines 1638-1652), the first navigated page is the adapter's partial watch page titled 'YouTube'. When that differs from prevTitle, it is said at once and titleWait is set to false. When it equals prevTitle (from home), the 2.5 s timer says 'YouTube'. Either way, the real title that comes later is never announced.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/index.ts, where navigated pages are announced, treat a page.partial page as not yet named. Set titleWait when page.partial or page.title === prevTitle. Have the timer and the 'titleWait && page.title !== prevTitle' branch announce only once the page is no longer partial. Also stop using the 'YouTube' placeholder as the title of partial watch pages in src/content/adapters/youtube.ts watch().

confirmed.fix: In src/content/adapters/youtube.ts, mark comment and description links that point to the current video with a t= value as seek links. Then, in the click-replay path in src/content/index.ts (afterAct or the link-click handler), scroll the player's portal placeholder into view after such a click. A more general option: after a replayed click, if the original window scrolled so that a portal's element came into view, scroll Sift's view to that portal.

confirmed.title: Settings dialog keeps the last sub-page's name ('Appearance', 'Display language') after Back or when reopened
confirmed.where: YouTube (any page), header Settings dialog and its sub-pages
confirmed.evidence: Settings, then Appearance, then Back: the dialog lists the top-level items ('Your data in YouTube | Appearance: Light | Display language | ... | Keyboard shortcuts | Settings | Help | Send feedback'), but its visible heading and aria-label stay 'Appearance' (3 of 3 runs). The original's ytd-multi-page-menu-renderer shows the top-level list at that moment. Escape from Display language, then reopening Settings: the dialog is named 'Display language' while it lists the top-level items (2 of 2). Screen-reader users hear the wrong dialog name. In 1 of 3 runs in this stale state, clicking 'Keyboard shortcuts' did nothing: no dialog opened, and focus stayed on the button. That did not reproduce in 2 retries. Shot: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-1/research/shots/R6T1-settings-back.png
confirmed.repro: cd /home/nico/projects/sift-test-1; SIFT_PORT=9461 SIFT_TAB=T1-youtube bun scripts/act.ts goto:https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ wait:12000 click:Settings wait:1500 click:Appearance wait:1500 click:Back wait:1500 "eval:(()=>{const d=[...document.querySelector('sift-root').shadowRoot.querySelectorAll('[role=dialog]')].find(d=>d.checkVisibility());return d.getAttribute('aria-label')+' | '+d.innerText.replace(/\s+/g,' ').slice(0,120)})()". It prints 'Appearance | Appearance Close Your data in YouTube Appearance: Light Display language...'. Also try press:Escape, click:Settings, click:'Display language', press:Escape, click:Settings, then the same eval: 'Display language | ...'.
confirmed.suspectedCause: The dialog's title is kept from the sub-page model when YouTube swaps the multi-page menu back to its top-level page (its header element stays in the DOM but hidden), so the title is read from a stale or hidden header.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced. Settings showed 'label=Settings'. Then Appearance showed 'label=Appearance', with Back and the theme choices. After Back, the dialog showed 'label=Appearance h2=Appearance' while listing the top-level items. The original at that moment: the top-level menu's visible #header is empty, and the only header with the text 'Appearance' is in the hidden submenu (checkVisibility false). Escape, then Settings again: the dialog was still named 'Appearance'. After Display language and Escape, reopening Settings gave 'label=Display language', with focus on Close. So the wrong name stays for the rest of the visit, and a screen reader announces it on open. The side claim did not reproduce: from the stale state, Keyboard shortcuts opened normally. The cause is in settingsMenu() in src/content/adapters/youtube.ts. `q("ytd-simple-menu-header-renderer", page)` searches the whole subtree of the top-level menu, so it finds the hidden submenu's header, and its h2 becomes the title.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/adapters/youtube.ts settingsMenu(), pick the header that belongs to the page being shown and is visible: qa("ytd-simple-menu-header-renderer", page).find(h => h.closest("ytd-multi-page-menu-renderer") === page && visible(h)). For the top-level page, the title then falls back to the opener's aria-label ('Settings').

confirmed.title: BBC at 600 px: a content map is dropped because its lazy image has no width/height attributes
confirmed.evidence: At 1280 px Sift shows 8 article images, including '[img] Map of the coast of Busan, South Korea, where a shark was spotted in a canal near Bukhang (North Port)…'. At 600 px it shows 7, and the map is missing (/home/nico/projects/sift-test-2/research/shots/r6t2-bbc-shark-600.txt). In the original at 600 px that img has loading=lazy, src and srcset (ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/…), no width or height attribute, naturalWidth 0 and a 0 px rect. The F544 fix keeps lazy photos that carry size attributes (Jade, Faucher), but not this one.
confirmed.repro: Set the viewport to 600x900 (scratchpad t2/narrow.ts: bun narrow.ts https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c9zrdknlmpdlo 600 name 60000) and count shadowRoot article img elements: 7, with no 'Map of the coast' alt. At 1280 px the count is 8.
confirmed.suspectedCause: contentImage() still needs a rendered size or width/height attributes for a lazy image. An unloaded lazy with src/srcset and a meaningful alt inside the article body should be kept, for example at column width.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced 2 of 2 at 600x900. Both the Short version and the full text show 7 images, without 'Map of the coast of Busan…'. At 1280 px both show 8, with the map. The cause is not the one claimed. contentImage() already has a lazy fallback (generic.ts 1310-1316) that would keep a 568x0 lazy img with a 16:9 height. The map's figure holds two imgs. The first is BBC's grey-placeholder.png (aria-label 'image unavailable', 568x319.5, inside the figure's box). The second is the real lazy img (568x0, so it fails the 'framed' overlap test). figureImage() (~generic.ts 4671) narrows the list to framed imgs, which leaves only the placeholder. It skips the placeholder, then returns `best ?? imgs[0]`, which is the placeholder again. contentImage rejects that by LOGO_TOKEN ('placeholder' in its src), so the map is lost. A content map dropped at narrow widths also affects zoomed users. Medium holds.
confirmed.fix: In figureImage() (generic.ts ~4671-4695), filter out placeholder imgs (LOGO_TOKEN src, alt/aria-label 'unavailable|placeholder') before the 'framed' narrowing. Or ignore 'framed' when every framed img is a placeholder. Never return a placeholder as the `imgs[0]` fallback. Then contentImage's existing lazy 16:9 fallback keeps the real map.
